subject: Cave to Rhone large pit floor
text: A treasure chest on the large floor below corridor B contains the Thunder Sword.

evidence.quote: On this floor, you'll see a treasure chest two steps below you.  Open it to find the THUNDER SWORD.

subject: Cave to Rhone large pit floor
text: From the large floor, walking down then left leads to an invisible pit that drops you onto the chest's floor.

evidence.quote: Head directly down until you're two tiles away from the bottom wall, then walk straight to your left toward the wall that waits in that direction.  Just before you reach it, you'll fall into an invisible pit.

subject: corridor B
text: Walking right one step and then down one step from the corridor B staircase head drops you into a pit.

evidence.quote: From where you appear at the head of the staircase, walk right one step and down one step and you'll fall into a pit.

subject: corridor B
text: Corridor B has many pitfalls and it is easy to fall into one by accident.

evidence.quote: It's very easy to fall into one without intending to do so.

subject: Cave to Rhone corridor B
text: Partial map of corridor B marks the pits the author has found.

evidence.quote: Here's a map of the corridor, with the pits I've found marked.

subject: corridor B map
text: The corridor B map is incomplete and additional pits exist beyond those marked.

evidence.quote: Please note that I know there are additional pits, but I got through the dungeon before finding all of their locations.

subject: Beran
text: Warping back to Beran lets you save your progress.

evidence.quote: Warp back to Beran yet again to save this progress.

subject: pit fall
text: If you fall into a pit, you land on the floor below; walk to the right wall, follow it up to the staircase to the floor above.

evidence.quote: If you fall into a pit despite the map, you'll land on the floor below.  Walk to the wall to the right, then follow it up to the staircase that leads back up to the floor above.

subject: corridor B
text: From the point marked B, follow the mapped safe ground to reach the staircase up to the next floor.

evidence.quote: Now, walk left from that room and you'll appear at the point on the map I have marked as "B."  From there, follow the safe ground I mapped out to safely reach the staircase leading up to the next floor.

subject: Cave to Rhone final maze floor
text: Route: go right into the next room, through the J-shaped room, exit upper left then upper right, cross the large room to its right exit avoiding the upside-down L block, take the upper path, head up and fork left, take the upper path to the T, then head right to the exit staircase.

evidence.quote: Begin by walking along the path to the right, into the next room. ... There, you'll find yourself in a room shaped like the letter "J." ... Exit out the upper left and you're in another small room. ... Exit out the path to the upper right. ... This room is quite large, and for the most part you can just head to the exit on the right side of the room (just don't hug the wall near the block shaped like an upside-down "L" or you'll fall in a pit). ... In the next room, you'll see an upper and lower path. ... Take the upper one into another chamber, then head up along that path into the next room. ... Here, the path forks. ... Head to the left. ... In this next room, you should exit along the upper of the two paths, then follow that hallway to the "T" and head out to the right. ... Just keep heading right through the remaining rooms to reach the staircase that leads out of the dungeon.

subject: Thunder Sword
text: Thunder Sword is the most powerful sword and is used by the Hero.

subject: old man at Shrine of Rhone
text: The old man at the Shrine of Rhone revives or restores fallen party members for free.

evidence.quote: In the shrine, you'll find an old man who will revive or restore any of your fallen comrades without charging a cent.

subject: Shrine of Rhone
text: The old man at the Shrine of Rhone also tells party stats and saves progress.

evidence.quote: He'll also tell you your party's stats and save your progress.

subject: Shrine of Rhone portal
text: A portal in the Shrine of Rhone leads to the Underworld, which is the Alefgard already explored.

evidence.quote: There's also a portal you can take back down to what they call the Underworld, which is actually just the Alefgard you've already been exploring for most of the game.

subject: party
text: Before Hargon's Castle, level everyone in the party to at least level 20.

evidence.quote: you should level everyone in your party to at least level 20.

subject: hero
text: The hero should be closer to level 30 before going to Hargon's Castle.

evidence.quote: Your hero should be closer to level 30.

subject: Shrine of Rhone surroundings
text: Battle monsters just outside the Shrine of Rhone until your levels are high enough before going to Hargon's Castle.

evidence.quote: Instead of warping back, though, you'll want to spend some time just outside of the shrine, battling the monsters until your levels are high enough that you feel good about making the trek west to Hargon's Castle.

subject: Blizzard
text: Blizzards can cast a spell that instantly kills party members, which works best on the hero.

evidence.quote: Some of the worst monsters you can encounter are the Blizzards, which possess a spell that can instantly kill unfortunate party members. ... It's a cheap move and it seems to work best on the hero, though don't be surprised if it occasionally takes out the prince or princess.

subject: Blizzard
text: Blizzards are best attacked with fire-based spells in the first turn, then physical attacks in the second round.

evidence.quote: These creatures are best assaulted with a robust selection of fire-based spells in the first turn.  Then you can clean up in the second round with physical attacks (particularly if, like me, you have the prince equipped with the Falcon Sword and its two strikes per turn).

subject: Giant
text: Giants have large life meters and strikes that deal a lot of damage.

evidence.quote: The giants have large life meters and their strikes definitely do a lot of damage.

subject: Gold batboon
text: Gold batboons can put you to sleep with breath and also breathe scorching flames that deal heavy damage.

evidence.quote: The gold batboon monsters can put you to sleep with their sweet breath, and they also breathe scorching flames that can quickly do a lot of damage.

subject: Gold batboon
text: Physical attacks are the best bet against gold batboons.

evidence.quote: Some fierce physical attacks are your best bet against them.

subject: Bullwong
text: Bullwong uses the Explodet spell, which hits the whole party for around 50 damage.

evidence.quote: Meanwhile, the bullwong uses the lethal Explodet spell, which can hit everyone in your party for around 50 points worth of damage.

subject: Bullwong
text: Bullwong has a huge life meter and spells that try to nullify his magic almost never work.

evidence.quote: He also has a huge life meter, and spells attempting to nullify his magic almost never work.

subject: Bullwong
text: Putting Bullwong to sleep is the suggested solution.

evidence.quote: The solution?  Try putting him to sleep.

subject: Guardians
text: Three guardians must be defeated before reaching Hargon.

evidence.quote: Before reaching Hargon, you'll have to face three guardians.

subject: Guardians
text: Defeated guardians stay gone until you save and power off the system.

evidence.quote: When you defeat them, they'll stay gone for good until you save and power off the system.

subject: Guardians
text: Do not attempt anything in Hargon's Castle until you have leveled up sufficiently.

evidence.quote: The implications of this are obvious: don't attempt anything until you've leveled up sufficiently.

subject: Guardians
text: The Repel spell should make the guardians quick to finish.

evidence.quote: It may take a few trips through the castle, but the Repel spell should make them quick.

subject: Hargon's Castle electrified floor
object: gray tile with Eye of Malroth
text: Walk north to the throne, Stepguard onto the candy-striped floor, use the Jailer's Key on the left gray wall, Stepguard again to the golden-key door on the right, then Stepguard to the gray tile and use the Eye of Malroth.

evidence.quote: Begin by walking north toward the throne, where two purple monsters stand. ... Cast the spell of Stepguard, then walk onto the candy-striped floor behind. ... Head to the left side, face the gray wall, and use the Jailer's Key. ... You'll need to cast Stepguard again, then head to the door to the right. ... Use the golden key to open it, then step into the area beyond. ... You'll see a gray tile at the center of more of those electrified floors. ... Walk up to the tile (you'll want to use Stepguard magic yet again) and when you've arrived, use the Eye of Malroth.

subject: Jailer's Key
text: Use the Jailer's Key on the gray wall on the left side to open a hidden door into a hallway.

evidence.quote: Head to the left side, face the gray wall, and use the Jailer's Key.  This will open a door you didn't even realize was there, and allow you into a hallway behind it.

subject: Golden key
object: door to the right in the hallway
text: Use the golden key on the door to the right to open it.

evidence.quote: You'll need to cast Stepguard again, then head to the door to the right.  Use the golden key to open it, then step into the area beyond.

subject: Eye of Malroth
text: Use the Eye of Malroth on the gray tile at the center of the electrified floors.

evidence.quote: Walk up to the tile (you'll want to use Stepguard magic yet again) and when you've arrived, use the Eye of Malroth.

subject: Charm of Rubiss
text: Use the Charm of Rubiss after the inn to make the castle illusion melt away and reveal the dungeon.

evidence.quote: Once you've done so, use the Charm of Rubiss to make the illusion melt away.

subject: battle loss near Hargon's Castle
object: return to Shrine of Rhone with half gold
text: Losing a battle returns you to the Shrine of Rhone with half your gold for a free revival.

evidence.quote: If you run into bad luck (at this stage in the game, any encounter that goes awry could easily mean the death of you), you'll return to the shrine with half your gold for a free revival.

subject: Valley to Hargon's Castle
text: Monsters in the valley to Hargon's Castle give a bundle of experience points if beaten but are dangerous.

evidence.quote: The valley leading to Hargon's Castle is filled with all sorts of nasties that also happen to reward you with a bundle of experience points if you can beat them.
